[MUQATIL:32:12-14/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The criminals are Meccan unbelievers, who bow before God and plead to return to worldly life to do good because they are certain of resurrection.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An active participle for an action currently occurring or continuing functions like the present-tense verb in both meaning and government, taking its object in the accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a participle and a second noun share its genitive complement, both may be genitive; accusative coordination is also possible by eliding an understood verb or participle.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Jarir and Ka'b ibn Juayl provide poetic examples of accusative coordination understood through an omitted verb or participle.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If the action is completed rather than ongoing, the active participle has no tanwin and behaves like a noun, so a coordinated complement is genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusative coordination becomes stronger after a long separation from the participle's complement; Sībawayh cites والشمس والقمر حسبانا as Qur'anic evidence. | mentions 6:96
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With a participle governing two objects, tanwin allows either object order; without tanwin, the complement joined to the participle cannot be separated, as in مخلف وعده رسله. | mentions 14:47
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetic examples, including Zuhayr's تنوين on سابقا, show the active participle with tanwin in this ongoing-action use.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Dropping tanwin or the sound plural nun for ease does not change meaning or make the participle definite; its object then takes genitive as it is joined to the noun.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh cites ناكسو رؤوسهم as an active participle without its nun in annexation, with its object in the genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Qur'anic examples such as ذائقة الموت, مرسلوا الناقة, غير محلي الصيد, and آمين البيت الحرام illustrate the uninflected participle construction. | mentions 3:185, 54:27, 5:1, 5:2
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | هديا بالغ الكعبة and عارض ممطرنا show the participle remains indefinite without tanwin, since it can describe an indefinite noun. | mentions 5:95, 46:24
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil gives هو كائن أخيك as a lightened form whose meaning is هو كائن أخاك.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh cites non-tanwined participles in poetry by al-Farazdaq, al-Zibriqan, al-Sulayk, al-Nabigha, and al-Marrar as evidence for the construction.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاضاربزيداغدا|فمعناهوعملهمثلهذايضربزيداغدا|#73/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · عيسى | reports | Isa reports that some reciters omit tanwin in Abu al-Aswad's verse to avoid two adjacent sukuns, not to make the participle genitive; Sībawayh calls this poetic necessity.
